messages:
maria: heads-up — getting an SLO alert for hosted-infer gateway in us-west-2. p99 timeouts and a spike in 5xx starting ~06:00 UTC. dashboard shows client-facing 504/502s. looks like a tail spike, not sustained.
obs-bot: [ALERT] SLO burn: hosted-infer.gateway p99 latency > 3s for 5m (us-west-2). error-rate 5xx=2.6% (baseline 0.3%). traces sampled=4% (low).
chris: copying logs now. any correlating deploys/rollouts in that window? kube events? can you paste the panel link?
maria: no deploys in the window. panel: https://console/redwood/dashboards/hosted-infer/gateway/overview?from=1749004000
kevin: I see increased connection resets from edge-proxy -> infer-pool on the same timeframe. kvcache evictions spike too. Could be prefetch/batcher starvation.
elaine: customer support: multiple customers reported 502s for sync generation requests. some mention auth failures earlier in traces — maybe token refresh? but logs show 5xx downstream.
maria: grabbing a sample log query — looks noisy. query:
```
index=prod-gateway source=gateway "status=5" | json | where(region=="us-west-2") | stats count() by status
```
result: 502 x 422, 504 x 181, 500 x 12. most 502s have downstream error "upstream reset".
chris: can you paste a raw request id from the 502s? need to check trace and proxy logs.
maria: req_id=rx7f9-usr-23. trace shows gateway -> edge-proxy -> pool-manager -> infer-node, then infer-node lost connection. no full spans after pool-manager.
kevin: that trace gap suggests TCP connection resets (handshake or OOM). checking infer-node logs: see repeated `runtime:signal: aborted` around matching times on a few nodes.
obs-bot: node-restart events: infer-node-3a terminated at 06:02:13 UTC, infer-node-4b terminated at 06:02:18 UTC.
chris: are these nodes on Dedicated? need to know if this is shared hosted infra or a tenant-dedicated pool.
maria: hosted shared pool (us-west-2 standard). not Dedicated.
elaine: billing/team note: two customers with reserved capacity also reported degraded performance — not just free-tier.
kevin: digging deeper — kernel logs show `oom_killer` invoked on infer-node-3a, process `inference-runtime` killed. memory pressure correlated with a sudden increase in batch sizes from traffic surge.
maria: any recent change to batching policy or model size? Optimize suggested a quant/rep config yesterday for a few routes.
chris: I don't see config pushes to production for batching since last week. could be traffic pattern change — some clients hit a long prefix that disables batching efficiency.
kevin: mitigation idea: temporarily enable aggressive max-concurrency cap on gateway for us-west-2 to limit batch sizes and reduce OOM risk. also remove large requests from the long-tail collector.
maria: can we throttle long-running sync requests at the edge and fallback to async with 429+retry-after? that would reduce pressure.
elaine: ops-approved message to customers: we're investigating a transient capacity issue in us-west-2 causing request timeouts. mitigating actions in progress. will update in 30m.
chris: I pushed a temporary gating rule to limit per-stream tokens=2048 and lower batch max to 8 for hosted pool in us-west-2. monitoring.
obs-bot: config-change recorded: gating-rule/limit-2048 applied at 06:10:12 UTC by chris.
maria: after change, 5xx dropping — 5xx now 0.8% and p99 latency back under 2.2s. traces still sparse but no new node restarts.
kevin: follow-up: need root-cause — why did batch sizes spike? collect client request distribution, look for single-tenant flood or automated crawler.
chris: ticketing: opening postmortem and follow-up action items: (1) add oom alerts on infer nodes, (2) add per-tenant rate tracking in datadog, (3) improve trace sampling when SLO burns. assigning owners.
maria: assigning (1) kevin, (2) elaine (with support), (3) chris. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate customer updates.
elaine: added customers A & B to the incident page. will send follow-up note once final RCA.
chris: one more: add a dashboard card showing batch size distribution and top request prefixes — would have flagged earlier. filing as action 4.
maria: thanks everyone — marking this thread for follow-up. if we see new restarts, ping @oncall immediately.
